title: Interpretation: PCA and t-SNE on synthetic data, images and recordings
promptMarkdown:
In under 350 words and without the notes open, compare three cases:

1. The simulated bivariate Gaussian data of W1D4 Tutorials 1–2 (stand-ins for two neurons' firing rates).
2. The MNIST handwritten-digit images of Tutorials 3–4.
3. A hypothetical single-trial population recording of several hundred neurons during a task (no such data are provided in this unit).

For each, say what a PCA scree plot and a two-dimensional t-SNE embedding can and cannot show, which assumptions of PCA hold or fail, and what you would need to know before calling any low-dimensional structure 'neural'. Say explicitly which of the three are neural data.
hintLadder: In the Gaussian case you set the covariance yourself, so PCA recovers exactly what you built in; that is a check of the method, not a finding.
MNIST has known categories, so an embedding can be judged by whether digits separate; images are not neurons.
For recordings think about Poisson variance, non-stationarity, single trials versus averages, and what variable defines 'relevant'.
t-SNE: neighbourhoods are preserved at the chosen perplexity; distances and cluster sizes are not.

deterministicChecks.description: when t-SNE is discussed, what it distorts or its perplexity dependence must be stated
when MNIST is discussed it must be identified as images, not neural data

criteria.criterion: Synthetic Gaussian: PCA recovers the built-in covariance exactly; linear-Gaussian assumptions hold by construction; the result is a check of the method, not a finding about neurons.

MNIST: images with known labels; the scree plot shows spread across pixels, reconstructions sharpen with K; t-SNE separates digits by neighbourhood but inter-island distances and sizes are not meaningful; nothing neural.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Missing the caveat or the non-neural point.

criteria.criterion: Recording: Poisson-like variance and rate differences dominate an unscaled covariance; non-stationarity and trial-to-trial variability mix with stimulus variance; single-trial versus averaged analysis must be stated; low-variance components may carry the task variable; structure is called 'neural' only after these are handled and the preprocessing is stated.

levels.label: met
levels.description: At least four of these issues.

criteria.criterion: States explicitly that only case 3 is neural data and that it is hypothetical in this unit.

checkExamples.label: correct explanation
checkExamples.text: Case 1 is synthetic Gaussian data standing in for two neurons: PCA recovers the covariance I set, the linear and Gaussian assumptions hold by construction, and the result checks the method rather than saying anything about neurons. Case 2 is MNIST, handwritten-digit images with known labels, not neural data: the scree plot describes spread across pixels, reconstructions sharpen as K grows, and t-SNE separates digits because it preserves local neighbourhoods at the chosen perplexity while distorting distances between islands and cluster sizes. Case 3, a hypothetical recording, is the only neural case and is not provided here: spike counts have Poisson-like variance so high-rate neurons dominate an unscaled covariance, non-stationarity and trial-to-trial variability mix with stimulus-driven variance, single-trial and averaged analyses answer different questions, and the task variable may live in a low-variance component; only after stating the preprocessing and checking these would I call the structure neural.

checkExamples.label: t-SNE distances read literally
checkExamples.text: t-SNE preserves the true distances between neural states, so islands far apart are very different states.
